Along the curved floor runs a park: a narrow stream, lawns, rows of young birch trees and low white residential buildings with terraced gardens. In the foreground at the bottom center, a child in a yellow raincoat rides a bicycle along a gravel path toward the viewer, while two adults sit on a bench to the right. Thin structural ribs of brushed metal arch across the ceiling at regular intervals, getting smaller with distance. Buildings on the far parts of the curve appear tilted and, near the top, upside down relative to the viewer. Soft, diffuse lighting, natural greens and pale greys, a calm Sunday morning atmosphere.

items.prompt: A bright, detailed concept-art illustration of a solarpunk coastal city on a summer afternoon, seen from an elevated hillside terrace so the whole city spreads out below toward the sea. summaries.A:
50 images, 303 checks. Mean score **4.22** (5: 19, 4: 23, 3: 8, 2: 0, 1: 0). Checks: **80.9% pass**, 15.8% partial, 3.3% fail.
Standouts: A001, A006, A016, A024, A035, A036, A043, A048.

All 50 renders are present, match the requested aspect ratio and are at least 14 MP. None looks broken.

## Pass rate by check type
age/body type/features 100% (n=19) · quoted text 100% (n=3) · props/wardrobe/setting 89% (n=91) · medium/style 87% (n=15) · face/expression 84% (n=25) · hand action/grip/handedness 78% (n=59) · body pose/limbs 75% (n=28) · mirror/reflection 71% (n=14) · light/camera/focus 70% (n=27) · finger/toe counts 55% (n=22)

## Failure modes
1. **The hand does the default action, not the one specified.** 9 images. Both hands grip the wok and the ladle is left untouched (A026). Double overhand grip instead of a mixed grip (A032). The middle finger is up, so the sign is not "I love you" (A038). The tattoo machine is held backwards with the needle pointing at the artist (A020). The left hand wraps the violin scroll instead of fretting (A025). The index finger is not on the shutter (A045). Both climber hands grip and there is no heel hook (A040). One hand is on the bowl instead of the tray (A002). The knot stage is vague (A041). Five of the 10 outright check fails in the set are this mode (A020, A026, A032, A038, A040).
2. **Digits where hands meet objects or other hands.** Finger and toe count checks pass 12 of 22. Fingers and toes merge into one tangle (A034). An extra hand grips the box lid (A004). A foot shows four clear toes (A017). The front hand is lumpy (A028), and so is a folded knuckle (A021). Counts cannot be confirmed in A005, A013, A031 and A047. Hands seen whole, in common poses, are clean: A006, A007, A009, A014, A015, A035, A036, A037, A043.
3. **Exact geometry.** The reflection's lipstick hand is on the wrong side (A022). The chord is not an open G (A005). The ollie board is tilted (A050). The Warrior III torso slopes upward (A012). Two front teeth are missing instead of one (A019). The flames bend sideways (A033). The sprinter's rear toe touches its shadow (A011).
4. **Small secondary details dropped.** No spike tape (A010). No motion blur on the skirt (A047). The lens flare is faint (A019). Light shafts are missing (A027) and caustics are faint (A018). The keyboard is full-size, not compact (A009). The red spot colour went on the shorts instead of the gloves (A030).
5. **Pseudo-text on surfaces nobody asked to have text.** Keycaps (A009), the bib header (A011), a T-shirt print (A023), mirrored lens-ring lettering (A045), mirrored fallboard lettering (A037), a scribbled signature (A046). Quoted strings render exactly: "417" (A011), "100" (A033), "R. OKAFOR, RN" (A043).

## What correlated with success
- Prompt length: 30 words or fewer, mean 4.83 (n=6). 90 to 120 words, 3.91 (n=11). 121 to 170 words, 4.17 (n=29). Over 300 words, 4.50 (n=4). Short prompts carry 5 checks with few constraints each. The 90 to 120 bucket contains three of the gesture failures (A034, A038, A030). The over-300 bucket is small, but A036 and A048 passed all 8 checks each.
- Medium: photo 4.21 (n=43), illustration 4.29 (n=7). No meaningful difference. All seven illustration styles read as their medium.
- Format: all 50 prompts are captions, so caption vs tags is untested.
- "hands:" subcategory: 4.00 (n=7) against 4.26 for the rest (n=43).
- Multi-mirror scenes held up (A024, A044, both 5). The single mirror seen from behind failed handedness (A022).
- Age, body type and skin features were never missed (19/19). Examples: centenarian A033, vitiligo A049, plus-size A023, powerlifter A032.

## Prompting advice
1. Expect a non-default hand configuration to fail even when every finger is spelled out. A005, A032 and A038 described the fingers one by one and still got the common shape. Plan an edit or inpaint pass for these. Whether a reference image helps is untested here.
2. Per-hand roles work when they match how the activity is usually photographed: tweezers (A036), kimchi (A048), needle and thread (A006), juggling (A035). They fail when the role is unusual: the ladle hand (A026), the climbing foot (A040).
3. Long, dense prompts are safe. A010, A025, A036 and A048 (339 to 346 words) average 4.50 and land most of their details.
4. Short quoted strings are reliable (3/3). If a visible surface should stay blank (keycaps, lens rings), say so. That fix is untested.
5. Check mirror handedness by eye whenever one body and its reflection are both in frame (A022).
6. Small edge details were missed or only partly rendered in A010, A018, A019, A027 and A047. Give them more weight if they matter. Whether that works is untested.

Standouts: B004, B005, B016, B026, B033, B034, B037, B045.

## Pass rate by check type
text 94% (n=16) · scene/style 90% (n=40) · spatial/position 88% (n=56) · attribute binding 84% (n=25) · counting 82% (n=62) · anatomy/integrity 76% (n=33, 0 fails, 8 partials) · action/interaction 71% (n=69)

## Counting accuracy
Headcounts of people and animals were exact in 39 of 44 checks. Object counts were exact in 12 of 18.

**1-4 (41 checks, 36 exact).** Exact: B001 2 people, B003 2 hands, B007 4, B009 2 + 1 dog, B010 2 + 3, B011 3, B013 2, B014 2, B019 1 + 4 dogs and 4 leashes, B020 3 cats + 2 dogs, B021 1 duck and 2 hens, B023 3, B024 3, B025 3 books, B027 4, B028 4, B029 2 mugs, B030 4, B031 2 + 1, B032 4, B034 4 children, B035 4 bikes, B036 3 children, B037 3 + 3, B038 1 + 2 + 1, B043 3, B044 4 + 1, B045 4, B047 4, B048 4, B049 2, B050 2 cups, B002 3 pears, B015 4 towers. Off: B012 2 boys plus 2 background players; B008 candles 4 → 5; B029 bars 4 → 5; B050 geraniums 3 → 5; B044 oars 4 → 8 (sculling rig).

**5-9 (18 checks, 13 exact).** Exact: B002 5 apples, B004 5, B005 7, B006 6 children + 1 adult, B008 6 people, B022 7, B026 5 animals, B029 5 people, B033 7 brown + 2 white, B034 6 candles, B042 5 graduates, B046 6, B050 6 windows. Off: B017 drummers 5 → 4; B021 ducklings 6 → 5; B036 balloons 9 → 7 (3/2/2); B039 front-row runners 6 → no distinct row; B042 caps 5 → 4 airborne + 1 held.

**10+ (3 checks).** B033 12 cups → 12; B041 15 singers in 3 rows of 5 → 15; B015 about 22 players → about 22, but lined up for anthems rather than kick-off.

Three of the four small-group misses rendered five (B008, B029, B050), and five was also the result when six ducklings were asked for (B021).

## Failure modes
1. **Moments of action replaced by a neighbouring pose** (action/interaction 71% pass, 6 fails, 14 partials). B011 shows a handball instead of a kick, with no slide; B013 the man's clasping hand is empty and the leg hook is missing; B031 the puck has already left the referee's hand; B027 the spiker's hand is behind her head, not on the ball; B010 free hands rest on the hip, not the table; B028, B040 and B049 swap the named pose for an easier one.
2. **Object counts drift by one or two.** B008, B017, B021, B029, B036, B050, plus the held cap in B042. Each of these images was otherwise strong; the count is usually the only miss.
3. **Equipment mechanics wrong.** B044 renders a sculling boat (two oars per rower), B030 a rope net instead of chain, B049 a canoe held one-handed by two women standing together mid-hull, B047 a board with pieces still near their home ranks.
4. **Attributes dropped on part of a group.** B041 men wear no burgundy scarves; B003 the young woman's hand is elderly and the same tone as the man's; B048 the knight wears a second helmet.
5. **Anatomy holds but has soft spots.** No anatomy fails. Partials: B009 overlong leg, B013 an extra hand with no arm, B043 the boy's arm emerges from behind the rack, B018 a bare foot in the crowd.
6. **Text is reliable except in a dense long scene.** 15 of 16 quoted strings correct. The one miss is B017 ("SUMMER LANTTEN FESTTVAL", 305-word prompt). Unrequested text is gibberish: B011 shirt names, B039 identical bibs, B044 hull.

## What correlated with success
- **Prompt length:** under 40 words n=5 mean 4.00; 90-119 n=25 mean 4.12; 120-169 n=16 mean 4.12; over 300 n=4 mean 3.75 (74% check pass). The end buckets are small.
- **Medium:** illustration n=7 mean 4.29 (86% pass); photo n=43 mean 4.05 (81%).
- **Format:** all 50 prompts are captions, so caption vs tags is untested here.
- **Digits vs words for numbers:** digit prompts n=5 mean 3.80 (B021, B029, B036 missed counts); word prompts n=45 mean 4.11. Small n and confounded with subject.
- **Scene type (my own post-hoc grouping):** static posed groups n=13 mean 4.92 (96% pass); crowds n=7 mean 3.71 (74%); sports or dynamic action n=10 mean 3.50 (72%).
- **Aspect ratio:** no pattern; 9:16 n=2 mean 3.00 is too small to read.

## Prompting advice
1. Headcounts up to 15 are dependable (B005, B022, B041). For counts of small objects or animals, check the output and regenerate; four of the seven count misses rendered five when 3, 4, 4 or 6 were asked for (B008, B021, B029, B050).
2. Describe an action as a visible state rather than a moment ("the puck pinched between his fingers", "her right foot follows through across her body"). Untested; based on the action failures in B011, B027 and B031.
3. Name the rig or mechanism when it matters ("sweep oars, one per rower, alternating sides"; "one woman under each end"). Untested; based on B044 and B049.
4. Repeat a group attribute for every subgroup ("the men also wear burgundy scarves"). Untested; based on B041.
5. Short quoted text is safe. In long, busy prompts keep banner text short and say it is large in frame. Based on B017 only.
6. If extra people would break the brief, say "no one else in frame". Untested; B012 added two background players.
